areas.label: Availability
areas.note: If this is red the server is down or a database is not usable — nothing else matters first.

areas.label: CPU
areas.note: Sustained high CPU makes every query slower; check the top process and the heaviest queries.

areas.label: Memory
areas.threshold: WARN ≥ 85% · CRITICAL ≥ 95% used · PLE < 2000 s = pressure (report rule)
areas.note: Low page life expectancy means the buffer pool is churning: pages are read from disk again and again.

areas.label: Disk space
areas.note: A full data or log volume stops writes: the database goes read-only or the instance stalls.
areas.capacity: C: 42.5 / 99.4 GB used / total · 56.9 GB free · 3 volumes, 702 GB free of 799 GB

areas.label: Disk latency
areas.threshold: WARN ≥ 20 ms · CRITICAL ≥ 50 ms — report rule, the collector logs only. Cumulative since engine start, not interval latency
areas.note: Latency above ~20 ms per read means storage, not SQL, is the bottleneck. This value is an average since SQL Server started, so it describes the history of this instance's storage, not necessarily its state right now.

areas.label: Storage activity
areas.threshold: WARN queue length ≥ 2 per spindle — throughput and IOPS are logged, not judged
areas.note: How hard the storage is being worked. A high queue with low throughput is a storage limit; high throughput on its own is just a busy server.

areas.label: Blocking
areas.threshold: WARN any blocked session · CRITICAL ≥ 10 blocked or blocked ≥ 300 s
areas.note: One session holding a lock can stall an application entirely; find the head blocker.

areas.label: Long-running queries
areas.note: A query running for an hour is usually a missing index, a bad plan, or a runaway job.

areas.label: Backup
areas.threshold: per-database policy: required FULL/DIFF/LOG age from data/backup_policy.json
areas.note: Backup age is your worst-case data loss. A stale log backup means point-in-time recovery is not possible for that database.

areas.label: Failed jobs
areas.threshold: WARN any job failed since the last run
areas.note: A failed maintenance job is a backup, an index rebuild or a purge that silently did not happen.

areas.label: TempDB
areas.threshold: WARN ≥ 85% used and < 2 GB free · CRITICAL ≥ 95% used and < 1 GB free
areas.note: TempDB filling up fails sorts, hashes and version store — often a single bad query.

areas.label: Security
areas.threshold: no sustained failed logins · no password older than the collector's threshold · no certificate expiring
areas.note: Thousands of failed logins a day is a credential being guessed or an integration retrying a dead one — and it fills the error log either way.

areas.label: HA / replication
areas.threshold: every replica CONNECTED and SYNCHRONIZED / streaming
areas.note: A replica that stopped synchronising is not a replica: failover would lose data. AVAILABILITY_DATABASE_HEALTH reads Availability Groups, database mirroring and log shipping (2008 R2 too, since 0.30.0) — on a Failover Cluster Instance with none of them it reports NOT_CONFIGURED, which is not an FCI health verdict.
